subject: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cognimed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a scoped eval running on Redwood: 

Summary of ask:
- You want an automated triage assistant for triaging incoming clinical notes and routing them to the correct specialty team.
- Primary metric: correct triage label (top-1) + calibration on urgency score for high-risk cases.

Redwood recommended model shortlist (based on today's workload signal):
- Redwood-2-7B (FP16 -> 4-bit quant for faster inference, aggressive KV caching) — fastest latency, good for low-cost burst traffic.
- LlamaX-13B-4bit (recommended for broader instruction-following on messy notes) — slightly higher cost but better recall on rare classes.

What we'll run for customer-specific evals on Redwood:
1) Ingest sample dataset you provide (see required schema below).
2) Run 3 model variants across the same prompt bank: Redwood-2-7B-quant, LlamaX-13B-4bit, and a small distilled baseline (for cost baseline).
3) Scoring: top-1 accuracy, precision/recall per label, urgency AUC, and regression monitoring against your production baseline.

Attachments I've included:
- cognimed_prompt_set_v1.csv (initial prompt bank derived from call)
- redwood_eval_scoring_template.xlsx (scoring sheet we will use)
- dataset_schema_ndjson.jsonl (required fields and examples)

Immediate asks for your team:
- Send a 2k–5k sample of de-identified notes in the NDJSON schema by EOD Tuesday (2024-04-16).
- Confirm if any labels need to be merged (you mentioned "med-admin" + "care-coordination" might be combined).

If that sounds good I'll schedule the kickoff run (2–3 day run, then a scoring pass). Ben and Marissa will lead the bench and scoring.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

From: Elena Morris <elena@cognimed.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Cognimed Data Science <datasci@cognimed.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template

Thanks Jasmine — this is great and matches my notes. A few clarifications: 

- We'll provide ~3,200 de-identified notes (NDJSON) by Monday 4/15 EOD.
- Label schema: we can merge med-admin + care-coordination into a single "Coordination" label.
- For urgency calibration: we have an internal 0-1 score; we'll include that as metadata per record.

One ask: can Redwood include an automated regression check that alerts if model recall on "HighRisk" drops more than 6% vs baseline? That's our hard stop for rollout.

I attached a short internal doc with label definitions (sent separately to Marissa).

—Elena
Elena Morris | Head of Data Science, Cognimed
elena@cognimed.ai | +1 (617) 555-1224

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template

Jasmine / Marissa — quick internal notes so we're aligned on run config: 

- Data format check: ensure NDJSON has fields: id, note_text, label, urgency_score (0-1), source_date. I'll run a lightweight validator when we ingest.
- Evaluation split: 70/15/15 (train/val/test) — but for benchmarking we'll keep the same test holdout across models.
- Prompt strategy: two templates in cognimed_prompt_set_v1.csv: a single-shot routing prompt + a clarification prompt for ambiguous notes. We'll try both and surface which prompt yields the highest recall for HighRisk.
- Scoring thresholds: set recall baseline from their historical model (they sent numbers to Marissa). We will implement the 6% regression alert as an automated regression rule in the Redwood Console (alerts + Slack webhook).

I'll prepare the job YAML and a runcard. ETA to you: EOD Friday 4/12.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@cognimed.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template

Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround. We received the dataset link this morning (thanks) and Marissa confirmed the label defs look good. Next practical steps: 

- Kickoff & baseline run: Monday 4/15 09:00 PT — Ben will trigger the ingestion and run the three model variants; expect ~48 hours for full runs + scoring.
- Deliverables after run: per-model CSV of predictions, the filled redwood_eval_scoring_template.xlsx, and a short deck with recommended model for production and quantization profile.
- Regression automation: we'll wire the 6% recall alert to your Slack channel #cognimed-alerts and to your PagerDuty if you'd like (confirm).

Scheduling: here's a calendly for the kickoff if you need to update timing: https://calendly.com/redwood/kickoff-30m

I've attached the dataset_schema_ndjson.jsonl again and a refined prompt set (v1.1) — small clarifications to handle edge-case abbreviations. 

On the internal side Ben — once you have the job YAML, also include memory/quant settings for Redwood-2-7B-quant; we want a trial with prefix cache enabled and batch size tuned for 100 tokens average.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@cognimed.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: Cognimed model-fit action items & eval template

Quick technical confirmation: we will run with these exact scoring bins in redwood_eval_scoring_template.xlsx — Top1, Top3, Macro-F1 by label, Urgency AUC, and a separate confusion matrix for HighRisk vs others. Regression alert will compute moving-window recall over the last 30 runs and compare to baseline recall; alert threshold = 6% absolute drop.

Notes for ops: Redwood-2-7B-quant run profile: 4-bit quantization, KV prefix cache ON, batch=12 for inference (estimate tokens per note = 150). LlamaX-13B-4bit profile: batch=8, prefer fp16 kernels for a hybrid path. Baseline distilled model: small CPU-backed run for cost comparison.

I'll post the run YAML and the job ID to the HubSpot activity and Drive link after the kickoff.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
summary: Sales follow-up thread with Cognimed to run customer-specific evals on Redwood. Includes model recommendations, dataset schema and prompt set attachments, scoring criteria (Top1/Top3/Macro-F1/Urgency AUC), and an automated regression alert (6% recall drop). Kickoff scheduled for 2024-04-15; Ben to provide job YAML and run artifacts.
